import { Aside, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import SeqDiagram from '../../../../components/SeqDiagram.astro';

**Task:** call a service outside the cluster (a captcha check, a payment
API, a model, any HTTPS API) and write what it answers into state.

A call may ask its node for **one** HTTPS request. The node makes it only when
every gate below holds and answers with its reason otherwise. Outbound requests
are **off by default**: an app that needs them runs on a cluster whose operator
turned them on, for its hosts or for any host an app declares.

## The gates

| Gate | Who sets it |
| --- | --- |
| `[outbound] enabled = true`, and the request's host is in `hosts` (or `hosts` holds `"*"`: any host an installed app declares) | The cluster's operator |
| The request's URL is under a prefix in the app's signed release manifest (`outbound`): the same host, and the prefix's path or one below it at a `/`, with any query string | The app's publisher |
| A prefix covering the URL is approved for the app's publisher | Whoever holds `MANAGE_APPLICATION` org-wide in the app's organization (its owner and admins; a member granted it), its personal organization included; the operator where the cluster was deployed with `--outbound-approvals operator` |
| The run is a call that writes: not a view, an `init`, a migration, or a call by a read-only member | The node |
| One request per run; `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`; `https` on port 443 to a DNS name that resolves only to public addresses; no fragment; no redirect followed; no proxy | The node |
| Request body ≤ 64 KiB, URL ≤ 2 KiB, ≤ 8 headers of ≤ 1 KiB, response body ≤ 1 MiB (a longer one is refused, not cut), 10 s for the whole request | The node (`calimero_primitives::outbound`) |
| `Host`, `Cookie`, `Connection`, `Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Proxy-*` and `X-Forwarded-*` headers are refused | The node |

A refusal is an `AppError` with code `Fetch` and a `message` field. A refusal
for a missing approval starts with a stable word an app can match on:

- `NotApproved:` nobody approved the prefix the URL is under. Nothing was ever
  approved for this publisher, or the owner saw the prefix and left it out or
  revoked it. Tell a member to ask the owner.
- `AwaitingApproval:` a later release of the app declares the prefix and the
  owner has not been asked about it yet. The prefixes approved before keep
  working. Show the owner what to approve.

A run with no outbound client at all (outbound is off, the app is not a signed
release declaring a prefix, or the run is not a writing call) and a second
request in one run trap the run.

## Secrets

The app never holds a secret. A request names one as `{{secret:NAME}}` in a
header value or the body; the node fills it in from **its operator's**
secrets, for this app only (the package and signer of the installed release,
never anything the app says), and only into a request to a host the operator
bound that secret to. Any copy of it in the response is replaced with
`[redacted]` before the app sees the response. So a method cannot write the
secret into state, where it would replicate to every member.

<Steps>

1. Declare the URL prefixes in the release's `manifest.json`, under
   `outbound` (`calimero_bundle::BundleManifest::outbound`). They are signed
   with the rest of the manifest and shown to whoever approves them, so
   declare the narrowest that works. Each is `https://` with a host and no
   credentials, query or fragment; the node refuses a bundle with any other:

   ```json
   "outbound": [
     "https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify",
     "https://api.stripe.com/v1/"
   ]
   ```

   `https://api.stripe.com/v1/` covers every path below `/v1/`.

   <Aside type="caution">
   Core's `scripts/pack-component.py` has no flag for `outbound`, and nothing
   in core reads it from `Cargo.toml`. Whatever writes your manifest must add
   the field before `mero-sign sign`; check the packaging tool you use.
   </Aside>

2. Make the request from a method that writes, and store the decision:

   ```rust
   use calimero_sdk::action::Request;

   /// Whether Cloudflare Turnstile accepts `token` (`apps/v2-fixtures/captcha`).
   pub fn verify_turnstile(&mut self, token: String) -> app::Result<bool> {
       let body = format!(
           "secret={{{{secret:TURNSTILE_SECRET}}}}&response={}",
           form_escape(&token)
       );
       let request = Request::post(TURNSTILE_VERIFY_URL, body)
           .header("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded");
       let Ok(response) = env::fetch(&request) else {
           return Ok(false); // an unreachable verifier is never a pass
       };
       Ok(response.status == 200
           && response.json::<Siteverify>().is_ok_and(|answer| answer.success))
   }
   ```

3. Have the owner approve the prefixes (see [approving](#approving-the-prefixes)),
   and the operator allow the host and supply the secret (see
   [the operator's side](#the-operators-side)).

</Steps>

<Aside type="caution" title="Only the leader asks">
The request runs once, on the app's leader, which runs the call. The other
replicas apply the diff the call wrote; they never repeat the request and never
see its response. Store the decision, not the response.
</Aside>

## Approving the prefixes

The organization's data is what a call can send, so the organization agrees to
the hosts too: the operator allowing a host and the publisher declaring it are
not enough. Someone holding `MANAGE_APPLICATION` org-wide approves with a
passkey step-up over the exact change:

```http
POST /orgs/{org}/outbound
{ "package": "com.acme.forms", "prefixes": "manifest" }
```

`"manifest"` (the default) approves every prefix the package's latest release
declares; a list approves those. An app that declares no `outbound` needs and
asks for nothing.

- **Per publisher.** The approval is keyed by the package's pinned signer, so
  a release signed by someone else starts with nothing approved.
- **Per organization.** It holds for every app of the package in the
  organization. An app created without naming an organization is in its
  owner's personal organization, approved the same way on
  `/orgs/{personal org}/outbound` (there are no per-account approvals since
  1.0.0-rc.20).
- **Releases only add.** A prefix a later release declares that the owner was
  never shown answers `AwaitingApproval` until approved; the rest keep working.
- **Revoke by setting the list.** `"replace": true` sets the publisher's list
  exactly; an empty list with it revokes everything. It holds from the next
  call.
- **Operator-governed clusters.** A cluster deployed with
  `--outbound-approvals operator` takes approvals from its operator instead,
  for every app: `POST /ops/outbound` with the same body, over the Ops API.
  The owner's route then answers that the operator holds them.

With `meroctl`: `namespace outbound <org> --package <pkg> [--prefix <p>]… [--replace]`,
and `account outbound --package <pkg> …`, which does the same on the account's
personal organization. On a development cluster add `--dev-passkey <file>` to
approve the step-up.

An app's frontend can also ask for the approval on the node's consent page
(`POST /consent/requests` with `kind: outbound`), where the person approves
with their passkey.

## The operator's side

The `[outbound]` table of `merod`'s configuration, or of the file
`--settings` names (which replaces it). Give every node of a cluster the same
table: the call runs on the app's leader, whichever node that is.

```toml
[outbound]
enabled = true
hosts = ["challenges.cloudflare.com", "api.stripe.com"]   # or ["*"]

# Secrets from environment variables, read once at start: a missing one
# fails the start.
[outbound.env_secrets.TURNSTILE_SECRET]
env = "MERO_TURNSTILE_SECRET"
packages = ["com.calimero.mero-forms"]
signers = ["did:key:z6Mk…"]   # the package's signer
hosts = ["challenges.cloudflare.com"]
```

`hosts = ["*"]` lets every installed app reach the hosts its own signed
manifest declares and its owner approved, so a new app needs no config
change. Every other gate still holds, and a secret still goes only to the hosts
bound to it.

Instead of `env_secrets`, a node can ask a secrets service beside it
(exclusive with `env_secrets`):

```toml
[outbound.sidecar]
url = "http://127.0.0.1:7070/v1/secret"
token_env = "MERO_SECRETS_TOKEN"
```

The node `POST`s `{"package", "signer", "name"}` with the token as a bearer and
expects `200 {"value", "hosts"}` or `404`. The URL must be `http` on a loopback
address. A managed deployment answers there with the secrets a deployer set
for their app, so the secret lives on the nodes that serve the app and nowhere
else.

The node logs every request it makes or refuses, with the app and the URL,
never the secret, and counts the requests it sends
(`calimero_app_outbound_requests_total`).

A secret is matched on both the package and the release's signer: anyone can
name a package, only its publisher can sign it.

## Test it

`env::fetch` needs a component: on the host target it answers an error. In
`TestApp`, `mock_http(..)` answers it in every run, so a test sets the response
it wants and checks what the app decided ([Testing](/build/testing/)).

End to end, use a node built with `--features calimero-node/outbound-testing`:
the scenario runner's in-process nodes are, and so is
`cargo build -p merod --features calimero-node/outbound-testing`. Its
`[outbound.testing]` table, which a release build refuses, answers `.test`
hosts in-process and takes literal secrets. A scenario gives its nodes that
TOML as `cluster.settings`:

```toml
[outbound]
enabled = true
hosts = ["echo.outbound.test"]

[outbound.testing]
echo = true          # .test hosts are answered in-process

[outbound.testing.secrets.ECHO_KEY]
value = "s3cr3t-e2e"
packages = ["com.example.my-app"]
signers = ["did:key:z6Mk…"]
hosts = ["echo.outbound.test"]
```

The echo answers `200` with the request the node sent, as JSON: method, URL,
path, query, headers, body and the number of secrets filled in. It answers only
after every gate has passed, and its answer is redacted like any other, so a
scenario sees exactly what left the node. The node's cluster tests use it
this way: `actions_run_on_the_leader_and_reach_only_declared_approved_hosts`
(declared and approved prefixes, secrets, redaction) and
`a_call_checks_a_turnstile_token_through_a_captcha_service` (a call's
`env::fetch` through `apps/v2-fixtures/captcha`), both in
`crates/node/tests/component_cluster.rs`:

```bash
cargo test -p calimero-node --test component_cluster -- reach_only_declared_approved_hosts
```

## Retries and actions

`env::fetch` works from a call, a timer or a delivered xcall. The request goes
out once, from the leader, and the call's log entry records it with the
response, so a retry with the same idempotency key replays the answer instead
of fetching again (what a single-use token like Turnstile's needs). A timeout
or a refusal comes back as an error the call handles. Example:
`apps/v2-fixtures/captcha` (`verifyTurnstile`), a captcha service other apps
call synchronously ([Synchronous xcalls](/protocol/xcall/#synchronous-xcalls)).
Protocol detail:
[Outbound HTTP from component calls](/protocol/execution/#outbound-http-from-component-calls).

For work that needs several requests, or a request that should not hold up the
call, an `#[app::action]` runs outside the log on the leader: it fetches with
`ctx.fetch`, reads the app with `ctx.view` and writes through `ctx.call` to an
`#[app::allow(action)]` method. A call or timer starts one with
`env::start_action(method, &args)`
([Timers and actions](/build/guides/timers-and-actions/)).

## Where it stops

- A request never runs in a view. Read the answer back from state.
- Redaction removes the secret as sent. A service that answers with it
  encoded (base64, URL-escaped) defeats it, so bind a secret only to hosts that
  do not echo it.
- The response is not authenticated beyond TLS: a service you call can answer
  anything, so call only services you trust for the decision you store.
